Sun Dance
The original Crow Sun Dance, was used as a means of arranging the loss of a relative or friend through his spiritual favor and assistance. The Dance was not necessarilly an annual event, but when one was held it required total tribal effort and assistance. The end of intertribal warfare in part, also led to the end of the original Crow Sun Dance.
In 1941 the Shoshoni (Wind River, Wyo.) version of the Sun Dance was introduced to the Crow Reservation and has now become an annual event occurring at least once a year. However, original Crow Sun Dance songs are still sung and there are certain other characteristics of the modern version which are strictly traditional Crow.
In recent years the number of participants has increased substancially, and there have been members of various christian faiths also participating in the Sun Dance (including a Catholic Priest). The annual event requires much effort by many persons, certain individuals being appointed to perform given tasks. It is also necessary for the surrounding environment to be clean and undisturbed.
